newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OTTAWA BLANKS BUFFALO TO CLINCH FIRST PLAYOFF BERTH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OTTAWA BLANKS BUFFALO TO CLINCH FIRST PLAYOFF BERTH.

text.p: The Ottawa Senators officially ended their four-year reign as doormat of the National Hockey League by clinching their first playoff berth on Saturday.
After finishing with the worst record in the NHL its first four years in the league, Ottawa blanked the Buffalo Sabres 1-0 to secure seventh place in the Eastern Conference.

"No doubt, we're looking to go further," Senators coach Jacques Martin said. "If you look at our record in the conference in the second half, we're fourth. It shows we're a team that can make things happen. I think we're ready."

Steve Duchesne scored the game's lone goal with four minutes left and Ron Tugnutt needed to stop just 17 shots for his third shutout for the Senators, who finished with 31 victories -- 13 more than last season.
At the final buzzer, the team charged off the bench and mobbed Tugnutt, who had carried the club into the playoffs by going 9-2-1 down the stretch.
"In the third period, I had to keep telling myself to keep my eyes open because we had complete domination," said Tugnett, who faced only three shots in the final period.

Duchesne scored the most important goal in the Senators history, taking a pass from Alexei Yashin at the inside edge of the right faceoff circle and wristing a shot that beat Dominik Hasek on the stick side.
Hasek was his usual brilliant self in the Buffalo goal, stopping 33 shots, including 17 in the third period.
The two teams will meet in the first round of the playoffs.
In Montreal, the Canadiens clinched a playoff spot in their season finale and ended Philadelphia's shot at the top seed in the East by rallying for a 3-3 tie with the Flyers.

Vincent Damphousse scored the tying goal off a rebound with 13:56 to go in the third period as Montreal nailed down the eighth and final playoff berth in the East and a date with the New Jersey Devils in the first round of the playoffs.
Rookie Vaclav Prospal had a goal and an assist for Philadelphia. He put the Flyers in front 3-2 with his goal at 1:42 of the third. Rod Brind'Amour and Trent Klatt also scored for Philadelphia.
Saku Koivu and Turner Stevenson notched the first two Montreal goals.

In Toronto, Mats Sundin scored his 41st goal and Felix Potvin, playing in his team-record 74th game of the season, stopped 38 shots as the Maple Leafs beat the Calgary Flames 4-1 in the finale for two teams out of the playoff picture.
Sergei Berezin also tallied for the Maple Leafs, clinching the rookie goal-scoring title with his 25th of the season.
Joel Bouchard had the lone tally for Calgary, which concluded its season with four straight losses and a seven-game winless streak (0-6-1).
Sundin also had an assist and Leafs captain Wendel Clark scored an empty netter to finish the season with 30 goals.
In Vancouver, Donald Brashear and Markus Naslund each scored twice as the Canucks concluded a disappointing season with a 5-4 victory over the playoff-bound Edmonton Oilers.
Defenceman Steve Staios collected three assists for the Canucks, who missed the last playoff spot in the West by just two points despite closing on a three-game winning streak.
Vancouver, which reached the Stanley Cup finals in 1994, will miss post-season play for the first time in seven years.
Ryan Smyth scored his 39th goal for the Oilers, who went winless in their last four games (0-2-2).
At Washington, Kelly Miller and Calle Johansson scored 21 seconds apart in a four-goal second period as the Capitals skated to a 6-2 victory over the New York Islanders.
The win did not help the Capitals qualify for post-season play as Ottawa's victory kept Washington out of the playoffs for the first time in 15 years.
Dale Hunter and Craig Berube also scored for Washington in the second period. Peter Brondra picked up his 45th goal of the season for the Caps in the third.

In Los Angeles, Philippe Boucher scored twice and Ray Ferraro had a pair of assists as the Kings ended a seven-game winless slide with a 4-1 victory over the San Jose Sharks in a meeting of the two worst teams in the Western Conference.
"The third period couldn't run down fast enough," said Sharks coach Al Sims, whose team ended up with the second-worst record in the league behind Boston.
"It's just a terrible way to end the season, playing for nothing and obviously the Kings were doing the same thing."
